To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cDNA of the NADH-dependent plastid-localized enoyl- acyl carrier protein reductases from B. napus has been isolated and characterized and that it is a nuclear gene that is expressed during the phase of seed storage lipid biosynthesis.

we have cloned and expressed in Escherichiae coli the enoyl acyl carrier protein reductases from developing seeds of the oilseed crop B. napus, and have shown that the increase in the activity of this key enzyme during the phase of seed storage lipid biosynthesis is regulated at the transcriptional level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the enoy-ACP reductases of oilseed rape.
the isolation and characterization of the enoy-ACP reductases involved in the biosynthesis of storage lipids in B. napus.
the isolation and characterization of cDNA clones encoding a key enzyme in fatty acid biosynthesis in oilseed rape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B. napus enoy-ACP reductases are encoded by two gene pairs which are expressed in a developmentally regulated fashion during seed development.

the enoy-ACP reductases of B. napus are encoded by two pairs of genes, that the genes are differentially expressed during seed development, that the expression of the genes is not regulated by light or by the availability of substrates and that the increase in the activity of the enzyme during the phase of lipid accumulation is regulated by transcriptional control.
the B. napus enoy-ACP reductases are encoded by two gene families, each of them containing two members, and that the expression of the genes is developmentally regulated during seed development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
enoyl- reductase is a plastidlocalized enzyme which is synthesized as a precursor protein, which is translocated into the plastid and which is encoded by two pairs of genes in B. napus.

enoyl- acyl carrier protein reductases are a class of enzymes with an important role in fatty acid biosynthesis and that the regulation of their expression is an important factor in controlling fatty acid composition in oilseeds.
enoyl- acyl carrier protein reductases in B. napus are encoded by two pairs of homologous genes and that their expression during seed development is regulated at the transcriptional level.
